All peer workers are registered without suffrage filtering; notifyAll and vote pass/count only a boolean. The completion branch compares count with voter-derived threshold without a fresh lease check.

A successful nonvoter worker acknowledgement is counted by the same boolean tally as a voter; no suffrage check occurs between registration and threshold notification. This statement concerns local counting, not public API completion.

facts.meaning: The tenure-local commitment map records a monotonically increasing acknowledged log index for each currently included voter. Local storage completion, successful append replies with entries, and successful snapshot replies are distinct establishment paths.
facts.validity_context: Only configured voter keys participate; new leader creates a new map. Configuration replacement retains indexes of surviving voter IDs.
facts.durability: Volatile accounting over durable log/snapshot effects; acknowledgements themselves are not persisted.
facts.recovery: New tenure starts zero match indexes and reconstructs them through local dispatch and replication.

facts.meaning: The local commitIndex is the implementation-selected upper index for committed-log dispatch. Leader sets it from current-tenure quorum accounting; follower sets it from min(received leader commit, local last index). This fact records the selected bound, not proof that every local entry through it matches the leader.
facts.validity_context: Normal leader/follower append processing; follower selection follows term/predecessor checks and any replacement performed for this request. processLogs separately suppresses indexes already dispatched. For ordinary append catch-up with accurate metadata and a matching-prefix/divergent-suffix history, sender backtracking reaches the first conflict, which is truncated before dispatch; an arbitrary earlier matching batch is not established by that path.
facts.durability: Commit index is in-memory; log and snapshots supply persisted history.
facts.recovery: Startup reconstructs log/snapshot context; subsequent leader/follower processing learns commitment.
unknowns: Storage-error or snapshot-specific histories may invalidate the accurate normal-log metadata premise; their effect on the dispatch bound remains unresolved.

facts.meaning: A verifyFuture records one initial self vote and counts successful boolean notifications until reaching a voter-derived quorumSize, or signals early on a negative notification. The count itself carries no voter identity or suffrage evidence. Because registration includes nonvoter workers and vote receives only a boolean, successful nonvoter callbacks increment this count as well.

identity.context: leader tenure and registration in replication-worker notify maps

facts.validity_context: verifyLeader registers each multi-node verification with every existing replication worker; notifyAll clears each worker map before voting. The main loop consumes threshold notification and completes the same future; leader exit fails remaining registered futures.
facts.recovery: Not reconstructed; pending verification fails on leadership loss, and later callers allocate new futures.

facts.meaning: StableStore contains separately written lastVoteTerm and lastVoteCand values. A successful persistVote finishes both writes. A failure on the second write leaves the first write completed; requestVote reads the pair and treats term equality plus candidate-address equality as a repeated vote before checking log freshness.

identity.vote: stored term and encoded candidate address

facts.validity_context: Per-replica vote memory consumed by requestVote and written by electSelf/requestVote through persistVote. Separate calls have no interface-level transaction coupling. The fact records stored values, not a guarantee that the pair names one completed grant.
facts.durability: StableStore promises stable key storage; the two updates are separate fallible API calls.
facts.recovery: requestVote rereads stored keys; NewRaft restores current term but does not reconstruct or validate the vote pair.
unknowns: Fault-injected legal history and exact grant consequence need validation.

formation.explanation: Leader stores indexed current-term logs and reports its own match; per-peer replication verifies successful responses and accounts last sent entries or installed snapshot. Current voter majority and tenure startIndex select commit advancement. Leader propagates commit through append requests; followers check term and predecessor, reconcile entries, select a local bound and dispatch through processLogs. FSM execution is asynchronous; client success follows actual Apply completion. In ordinary accurate-metadata catch-up, end-first backtracking causes the first accepted conflicting request to truncate the suffix; receiver-only limited-batch reasoning does not establish an arbitrary early matching request.

context.explanation: Follower timeouts and transfer trigger campaigns over latest voters. Pre-vote checks plausibility without persisting term; actual election increments durable term, persists votes and uses log freshness. Campaign replies are private to the attempt. Leader entry creates fresh commitment and workers; higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss or self-removal ends authority, stops old workers and fails pending futures. Install/startup recover log/snapshot and configuration context; transfer catches target up before TimeoutNow.

connection.explanation: Support is eligible within the captured leader tenure and current voter set. Fresh tenure accounting and a current-term no-op prevent simply reusing old majority indexes; old workers retain old commitment/stepDown channels. Persisted history constrains votes, while a new leader reconciles follower suffixes before local consumption. Configuration changes are admitted one at a time after current-term commitment and immediately reinterpret voter support. Already dispatched FSM work is distinct from remaining inflight futures, so leadership loss cannot imply rollback. Snapshot recovery reinstates applied prefix/configuration and can supply catch-up support. In ordinary accurate-metadata catch-up, end-first backtracking causes the first accepted conflicting request to truncate the suffix; receiver-only limited-batch reasoning does not establish an arbitrary early matching request.

open_details: Ordinary accurate-metadata catch-up is explained by end-first backtracking and conflict truncation; storage-error and snapshot-specific histories remain separate questions.
VerifyLeader tally counts nonvoter callbacks; public completion and stale-read consequences remain separate from that local counting relationship
Storage errors between truncation/replacement and vote persistence writes
Concrete transport heartbeat concurrency and compatibility paths
Manual RecoverCluster and deeper snapshot compaction variants remain unmapped
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority acquisition/loss, old-work handling and recovery/consumption have been traced through actual producers and consumers. Local discrepancies remain questions and do not make these observed relationships guarantees.
